title: Draft: TCP: optionally dissect L5+ payload for retransmitted/duplicate segments
description:
Add a new "Dissect retransmitted segment payload (Layer 5+)" preference
under Protocols → TCP. Default off.

Today, when "Analyze TCP sequence numbers" is enabled, a TCP segment
flagged as a retransmission (or that overlaps an already-known
multi-segment PDU — e.g. a capture-level duplicate seen at a second
tap point) has its upper-layer payload silently skipped. The Info
column reads only "[TCP Retransmission] <seq/ack info>" with no L5+
detail (TLS, HTTP, etc.). The existing tcp.no_subdissector_on_error
preference governs only the non-desegmented code path in
process_tcp_payload; the three skip paths inside desegment_tcp are
unaffected by it.

When the new preference is enabled, retransmitted segments are still
handed to the upper-layer dissector via decode_tcp_ports() from each
of the three desegment_tcp skip points:

  * MSP-boundary match (segment seq range fits an already-known PDU)
  * TCP_A_OLD_DATA after non-OOO-reassembly retransmission detection
  * TCP_A_OLD_DATA in the OOO-reassembly path (when
    tcp.reassemble_out_of_order is also on)

The "[TCP Retransmission]" prefix in the Info column is preserved by
the existing col_prepend_fence_fstr() call in
tcp_sequence_number_analysis_print_retransmission(); the subdissector
output appears after the fence as expected.

Stateful sub-dissectors (DCE/RPC, some encryption schemes) may emit
misleading output if fed a replayed segment, so the preference defaults
to off; the existing skip behavior is unchanged for users who do not
opt in.

AI-Assisted: yes

notes.body:
[exampleForEugene.pcapng](/uploads/539814e5c7c8053fe074a67c17253acb/exampleForEugene.pcapng) here's a pcap that shows an example of retransmit with reassembled frames.

look at frame 8 and Try with option "Allow subdissector to reassemble tcp streams" on and off. with "analyze tcp sequence numbers" on. If that was not a reassembled stream then the "do not call subdissectors for errored packets" OFF would show that frame as a "client hello". But with a reassembled stream that option, and no other option allows for it to show as a "client hello" as long as your reassmebly streams.
